references.text: The people wept and longed for the food they had in Egypt, showing their rejection of the Lord's care.
The people complained again and wished to return to Egypt, reflecting the same attitude of contempt toward the Lord.
The Israelites complained to Moses and Aaron and expressed a desire to have died in Egypt, an early parallel to their rejection.
The psalm describes how God gave the people meat until they were full, but His wrath came upon them while the food was still in their mouths.
The people's craving in the wilderness and their testing of God, which resulted in Him giving them what they asked for, yet sending disease.
The people spoke against God and Moses and asked why they had been brought out of Egypt, the same pattern of contempt and complaint.
Isaiah speaks of a people who have rejected the Lord, parallel to Israel's contempt for God in the wilderness.
The Lord tells Samuel that the people have not rejected him, but the Lord Himself, a similar theme about rejecting God's presence.
